chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about touching the corner. He said: 'Touching it is pressing your belly against it, and wiping it is wiping it with your hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Istilam and Mas'h of the Rukn in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between 'Istilam' (pressing the body or hand against the stone) and 'Mas'h' (wiping), establishing the Black Stone as a sacred focal point for reverence. It reflects the Shia emphasis on precise ritual etiquette (Adab) in Hajj, where physical contact serves as a tangible connection to the Prophet’s tradition. The ruling underscores the stone's role not as an object of worship, but as a witness to the believer's devotion.
